cells.content: Performance Driven*Employees are encouraged to see failure as an opportunity to learn.
Clear Vision*Everyone is aligned on the same mission.
Embraces Failure*The best culture is driven by performance.
Values Your Time*No pointless meetings or unnecessary overhead.
Shows Empathy*Treats everyone with respect and empathy.
CI/CD pipeline*Deploy to production daily, not quarterly
Open Communication*Communication is two-way and clear across hierarchy levels.
Corrects Bad Behaviour*Bad behaviour is not tolerated and is corrected quickly.
Remote-first*Built around async/distributed work, not just "allowed"
Accepts Disagreement*Healthy debate is understood as critical for success.
Value Driven*Values are acted upon, not replaced by perks like bean bags or pizza Fridays.
Encourages Diversity*Looks for diversity of thoughts and perspectives.
Blameless postmortems*Incidents drive improvement, not punishment
Empowers Employees*People are trusted to make decisions and own their work.
Code review culture*PRs reviewed before merging to main
Competitive Salary*Compensation is fair and transparent.
Open source contributions welcome*Engineers publish under their own names
Structured onboarding*30/60/90 day plan for new hires
Conference budget*Learning & development allowance for growth
Transparent Promotion Path*People know how growth and promotion decisions work.
Real Work-Life Balance*Time away from work is genuinely respected.
Clear Budgets and Tools*People have what they need to do good work.
Remote-Friendly*Flexible location is a real policy, not a bait-and-switch.
Internal Mobility*People grow into new roles inside the company, not just out.
Internal tooling investment*Company invests in developer productivity
Clear Hiring Process*Timelines, steps, and expectations are communicated upfront.
Dodging salary questions
"We are a family"
Unpaid overtime
Entry-level, 3-5 years experience required*Senior work at junior pay
Unlimited PTO*Nobody actually takes vacation; untracked = unused
Mandatory pizza parties instead of raises
Salary is not listed in the job post
Time off is discouraged
"Rockstar" wanted*Expects one person to do the work of three.
"Thick skin" required*Criticism is frequent; feedback is not constructive.
Unpaid on-call work*You're available 24/7 but only paid 9-to-5.
Must be passionate about the mission*Emotional investment to compensate for low pay
No bureaucracy / minimal process*No documented workflows, tribal knowledge only
Equity instead of salary*"The startup equity will be worth millions" — it won't.
"Ninja" / "Guru" / "Wizard"*Overused titles masking unrealistic expectations.
We are scaling rapidly*Growth without infrastructure; you will be firefighting
No psychological safety*Mistakes are punished, not learned from.
"Young and dynamic" code*Age discrimination disguised as culture fit.
Micromanagement disguised as transparency*Every keystroke is tracked and reported.
Flexible hours + meetings everywhere*The flexibility is theoretical
Multiple rounds of unpaid interviews*5+ rounds before a decision — respect is absent.
Non-compete clause*You can't leave without losing your career for 2 years.
"Fast-paced environment"*Exciting for some, chaotic for others — depends on the team.
"Wear many hats"*Growth opportunity or scope creep? It depends on boundaries.
"Work hard, play hard"*Fun culture or an excuse for long hours?
"Hit the ground running"*Exciting challenge or zero onboarding?
"Self-starter" needed*Autonomy or abandonment? Depends on support.
"Startup culture"*Scrappy innovation or chaotic disorganisation?
Flexible working hours*Freedom to manage your time — or always-on expectations?
Flat hierarchy*Close to leadership or missing mentorship structure?
"Competitive environment"*Drives excellence or breeds internal rivalry?
Agile environment*Genuine iterative dev or just standups with no planning?
Startup mentality*Honest at 30 people, red flag at 500
Equity / stock options*Life-changing or worthless lottery tickets?
Move fast*Fine for MVP, dangerous for fintech/healthcare
On-call is shared by the team*Fair rotation or always-on?
Overcommitted deadlines*Ambition or poor planning?
Flexible work arrangement*Trust-based or policy changes every 6 months?
